summary: At the recorded base, UnifiedTreeNode.backuped means Full KV is present on host, and host-leaf eviction removes the node. The reported evicted-and-backuped L3-only stub state is therefore not representable. Added an end-to-end same-tree regression showing that partial eviction anchors at the repeated L2 prefix, complete eviction anchors at root, storage is actually queried, unavailable storage remains a miss, and restored GPU KV contains the original values.

tests.what_was_measured: The attempted issue-state assertion failed because partial host eviction removed the suffix leaf; last_host_node and best_match_node both identified the surviving repeated-prefix L2 node, rather than an L3-only stub.

Real file-backend partial and complete L1/L2 eviction, repeated-prefix anchoring, two L3 prefetch/load-back cycles, exact restored GPU key/value tensors equal to constants 23/24, and an unavailable-key miss.
The new same-tree regression at page sizes 1, 4, and 128, the existing fresh-tree L3 round trip, and the current host-leaf deletion invariant; 5 tests passed.

gpu_execution_evidence: Tests used the prepared torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 environment, loaded module_aiter_core from /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-ea02fcc8ae9a/cache/aiter/module_aiter_core.so, allocated GPU KV pools, and compared restored key/value tensors with independent constants 23 and 24.
remaining_limitations: The exact source-issue state could not be exercised on base 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365: UnifiedTreeNode.backuped is derived from a non-null Full host_value, while _evict_host_leaf frees all host/device component data and unregisters the leaf. Thus no node can remain both evicted and backuped after host eviction in this implementation. No server/model-scale reproduction was run because the prerequisite state is absent in the checked-out tree semantics.
